items.title: Helus Phase 3 efficacy contrasts with sharp intraday decline
items.summary: Helus reported a statistically significant 7.6-point placebo-adjusted depression-score benefit at Week 6, sustained at Week 12. A timestamped 10:01 AM ET quote showed HELP down 19.62% intraday. Safety, financing and confirmatory-trial risks remain.

observations.label: Clinical efficacy
observations.value: Week 6 MADRS placebo-adjusted -7.6 points, p<0.0001; Week 12 -7.0 points

observations.label: Risks and next checks
observations.value: Three treatment-related serious adverse events; full safety data, financing and EMBRACE replication

items.key_finding: Positive pivotal efficacy and sharp intraday weakness warrant monitoring safety and financing.

items.title: Uniper reports 700 MW secured grid access for potential data centers
items.summary: Uniper announced roughly 700 MW of secured grid capacity for potential European data-center development and about €6 billion in broader growth capex. Existing connections could shorten infrastructure lead times. Completed customer agreements and project economics remain unverified.

observations.label: November 16 company strategy update
observations.value: ~700 MW secured grid capacity; ~€6 billion broader growth capex

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Signed customer contracts, grid energization, permitting and capital returns; stalled contracts would weaken opportunity

items.key_finding: Secured grid capacity may be an increasingly valuable European data-center asset.

items.title: AI-sector selling broadens in US cash trading
items.summary: US chip and cloud-infrastructure shares extended their slide in Monday cash trading. The Nasdaq fell 2.1% at 10:15 a.m. ET, with AMD, Broadcom and CoreWeave weaker. Leadership and export-policy uncertainty are weighing on valuations ahead of Nvidia earnings, but weaker underlying chip demand is not yet established.

observations.label: November 16, 10:15 a.m. ET intraday snapshot
observations.value: Nasdaq -2.1%; S&P 500 -1.3%; NVDA -1.7%; AVGO -4.7%; AMD -4.7%; CRWV -6.4%; GEV -2.8% (AP); not closing prices

observations.label: Fundamentals
observations.value: Valuation, AI spending and governance concerns; customer order or shipment contraction not independently demonstrated

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: Nvidia earnings and guidance, export policy, chip orders, tech breadth and data-center project backlogs; resilient demand and price stabilization would weaken the selloff thesis

items.key_finding: AI-sector weakness has carried into cash-market trading, without proof of demand destruction.

sources.title: Financial Times US technology market coverage

items.title: Crude falls despite reported Hormuz tanker incident
items.summary: Brent declined in Monday morning trading despite UKMTO reports of a tanker strike and fire. Reuters reported recovering Hormuz shipments and a projected supply surplus. This is a price response, not independent proof that all shipping routes are secure or that the reported strike caused no cargo loss.

observations.label: Reported physical-flow context
observations.value: Reuters describes recovering Hormuz shipments; independently reconciled vessel and cargo counts unavailable in this pass

observations.label: Security evidence
observations.value: UKMTO reported tanker projectile strike and engine-room fire; incremental export loss remains unverified

observations.label: Next checks and invalidation
observations.value: UKMTO follow-ups, vessel identity and cargo, transit counts, insurance premiums, Brent/WTI settlements, IEA/OPEC data; confirmed export loss would challenge the recovery narrative

items.key_finding: Oil-price weakness and tanker security incidents coexist; actual export losses remain unverified.

sources.title: Reuters via Euronext: Middle East exports and oil outlook

items.title: Dell and HPE drawdowns contrast with reported AI infrastructure demand
items.summary: Barron's reported substantial declines in Dell and HPE shares since October 9 despite large reported AI server orders and improving infrastructure revenue. Their coming earnings provide a test of whether backlog translates into cash and margins. These are fundamentals-versus-valuation watch-list cases, not verified undervaluations.

observations.label: Cumulative share-price drawdowns reported November 16
observations.value: DELL about -41%; HPE about -34% since October 9 (Barron's); not single-day returns

observations.label: Reported company fundamentals
observations.value: Dell disclosed approximately $95B AI-server backlog; HPE reported $12.2B quarterly revenue and $1.0B free cash flow

observations.label: Risks and next checks
observations.value: Customer financing and concentration, backlog conversion, component costs, margins and free cash flow; HPE November 23 and Dell November 24 earnings; cancellations or weak cash conversion would weaken the thesis

items.key_finding: Large reported share-price declines warrant testing against backlog quality and cash conversion.

sources.title: Barron's November 16 Dell and HPE coverage
